## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: SIPDE, following distance, night driving, freeways, distraction, loads and trailers
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The night crash share and the distraction crash share are statistics printed in the manual that can change between editions; they are stated as printed and flagged (verify MN-DRIVEA-D-STATS) [A02] [A06].
The front seat rule is printed as a ban on driving with more than three people in the front seat or a load that blocks the view; the dossier keeps that exact wording [A07].
The trailer following distance is printed as at least five hundred feet; the dossier states it as printed and does not convert it to a time gap [A07].
The freeway merge steps and the cloverleaf, diamond, folded diamond and diverging diamond interchange designs are drawings; only their captions and the page text were used, and the drawings-only page carries no facts.
Headlight rules overlap with the vehicle chapter; the facts here are restated from this chapter's own page in fresh wording and add the low beam distances printed only here.

corpus_stability.reason: The Minnesota Driver’s Manual prints a single edition line (June 2026) on its front cover and opens with a New laws and information chapter that collects recent changes in one place, with no sign of more than one rewrite per year in the selected pages.

verification_debt.claim_text: On physical page 76 the Minnesota Driver's Manual (June 2026) says nearly half of fatal crashes in Minnesota occur after dark, and on physical page 81 that distraction accounts for at least 25 percent of crashes annually; both are statistics that can change and should be rechecked against current official DPS crash data before release.
